config.title: Modal & Action Sheet

intro.title: Modal & Action Sheet
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Ionic app that opens a modal window and an action sheet. You will learn how to use Ionic's ModalController and ActionSheetController to create and manage these UI components. The core programming concept involves using Angular services and asynchronous methods to present and dismiss overlays. You'll work with TypeScript to handle user interactions and data flow between components. By the end, you'll understand how to implement common mobile UI patterns for displaying additional content or offering choices.
intro.usecase: Modals and action sheets are essential UI patterns in mobile apps for presenting focused interactions without navigating away from the current screen. You'll see modals used for login forms, detailed item views, or confirmation dialogs in apps like Instagram or banking applications. Action sheets appear in messaging apps for selecting photo sources, or in productivity apps for choosing document actions like share, rename, or delete. As an Ionic developer, you'll implement these patterns to create intuitive, native-like user experiences that follow platform-specific design guidelines.

objectives: Apply Ionic modal component to create a reusable modal template in an Angular application.
Use the ModalController service to programmatically open and close modal windows.
Implement data passing between a parent component and a modal component using component properties.
Execute modal dismissal with optional return data to communicate user selections back to the parent.
Utilize the ActionSheetController service to create interactive action sheets with multiple options.
Construct action sheet buttons with different roles (destructive, cancel) to handle various user actions.
Define handler functions to process user selections from both modal and action sheet interfaces.
Access Capacitor platform utilities to detect the current device environment for conditional UI rendering.
Control modal presentation and styling by applying Ionic CSS custom properties and component properties.
Store and retrieve user preferences or selections using Angular services or local state management.
Modify component templates to include trigger buttons for both modal and action sheet presentations.
Compare usage scenarios for modals versus action sheets to choose the appropriate component for different user interactions.

steps.title: Import Ionic Angular core components and modules
steps.instruction: Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and IonContent, IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle, IonButtons, IonButton, IonIcon from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with the correct package paths. For '@ionic/angular/standalone', import each component individually.
steps.seedCode:
// Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core'
// Import IonContent, IonHeader, IonToolbar, IonTitle, IonButtons, IonButton, IonIcon from '@ionic/angular/standalone'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular and Ionic components are imported, enabling the use of Ionic UI components and Angular lifecycle hooks.
successCriteria: The import statements for '@angular/core' and '@ionic/angular/standalone' are correctly written with the specified symbols.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required Angular and Ionic components. These are essential for building the modal and action sheet UI.

steps.title: Import Ionic modal and action sheet controllers
steps.hint: Add an import statement that brings in both ModalController and ActionSheetController from the same Ionic Angular standalone package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Import Ionic modal and action sheet controllers
import { ModalController, ActionSheetController } from '@ionic/angular/standalone';
steps.expectedOutcome: The ModalController and ActionSheetController are imported and ready to be injected into the component.
successCriteria: The import statement includes both ModalController and ActionSheetController from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the controllers needed for modals and action sheets.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing both ModalController and ActionSheetController from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to import ModalController and ActionSheetController from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.

steps.title: Import Ionic icons
steps.instruction: Import the specific icon symbols 'add' and 'ellipsisHorizontal' from 'ionicons/icons' and import 'addIcons' from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.

steps.expectedOutcome: The code will have imports for the 'add' and 'ellipsisHorizontal' icons from ionicons/icons and 'addIcons' from @ionic/angular/standalone.
successCriteria: The import statements for icons and addIcons are correctly added.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required icons and addIcons. This will allow you to use these icons in your buttons later.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some imports, but check if both 'add' and 'ellipsisHorizontal' from 'ionicons/icons' and 'addIcons' from '@ionic/angular/standalone' are imported.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports for icons or addIcons are missing or incorrect. Make sure to import 'add' and 'ellipsisHorizontal' from 'ionicons/icons' and 'addIcons' from '@ionic/angular/standalone'.

steps.title: Create the main component class
steps.instruction: Create a new component class named HomePage with the @Component decorator, set standalone: true, and specify template URL './home.page.html'.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from '@angular/core' to define a new Angular component. Set the selector, standalone property, and templateUrl.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new HomePage component class is created with the correct Angular component metadata.
successCriteria: The component must be named HomePage, use the @Component decorator, have standalone: true, and specify templateUrl: './home.page.html'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the HomePage component with the proper Angular component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your component has all required properties: name HomePage, @Component decorator, standalone: true, and templateUrl './home.page.html'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't properly defined. Check that you're using the @Component decorator with the correct metadata.

steps.title: Implement OnInit interface
steps.instruction: Make the HomePage class implement OnInit and add ngOnInit() method.
steps.hint: Add 'implements OnInit' after the class name and define the ngOnInit() method inside the class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The HomePage class should implement OnInit and have an ngOnInit() method.
successCriteria: The code must include 'HomePage implements OnInit' and define 'ngOnInit()' method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the OnInit interface and added the ngOnInit lifecycle method to the HomePage component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the HomePage class explicitly implements OnInit and has the ngOnInit() method defined.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HomePage class needs to implement OnInit and include the ngOnInit() method. Check the class declaration and method definition.

steps.title: Inject modal and action sheet controllers
steps.instruction: In the ModalActionSheetPage class constructor, add parameters for ModalController and ActionSheetController with proper type annotations and private access modifiers.
steps.hint: Use the constructor parameters to inject the controllers as private class properties. The types should match the imported classes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ModalActionSheetPage class will have a constructor that properly injects ModalController and ActionSheetController as private dependencies.
successCriteria: Constructor should have two parameters with private access modifiers and correct type annotations (ModalController, ActionSheetController).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully injected the modal and action sheet controllers via the constructor. This is Angular's dependency injection in action, making these services available throughout your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your constructor parameters. Make sure both ModalController and ActionSheetController are included with private access modifiers and proper type annotations.
steps.feedbackWrong: The constructor injection isn't quite right. Review how to add parameters with private access modifiers and type annotations for ModalController and ActionSheetController in the constructor.

steps.title: Define method to open modal
steps.instruction: Inside the ModalActionSheetPage class, create an async method called openModal() that will open a modal dialog.
steps.hint: Add the method after ngOnInit() but before the closing brace of the class. Use the async keyword before the method name.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ModalActionSheetPage class now has an empty async openModal() method ready for implementation.
successCriteria: The method must be async, named 'openModal', and placed inside the ModalActionSheetPage class.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the openModal() method. This async method will be used to present a modal dialog in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure the method is named exactly 'openModal', uses the async keyword, and is placed inside the ModalActionSheetPage class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The openModal() method wasn't created correctly. Check that it's an async method inside the ModalActionSheetPage class with the exact name 'openModal'.

steps.title: Define method to open action sheet
steps.instruction: Inside the ModalActionSheetPage class, create an async method called openActionSheet() that uses the injected actionSheetController to create and present an action sheet. The method should use actionSheetController.create() with at least one button configuration and
steps.hint: Use the async keyword before the method name. Inside the method, call this.actionSheetController.create() with an object containing a 'buttons' array. Then call .present() on the result.
steps.expectedOutcome: The ModalActionSheetPage class now has an async openActionSheet() method that creates and presents an action sheet using the injected ActionSheetController.
successCriteria: The method must be async, named openActionSheet, use this.actionSheetController.create() with a buttons array, and call .present() on the created action sheet.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the openActionSheet method. This method will allow you to present an action sheet when called.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Is the method async? Does it use this.actionSheetController.create() with a buttons array? Does it call .present() on the result?
steps.feedbackWrong: The openActionSheet method is missing or incorrect. It should be an async method that creates an action sheet using this.actionSheetController.create() and presents it.

steps.title: Create the component template structure
steps.instruction: Add a button inside the ion-content to open the modal and another button to open the action sheet. Use the existing openModal() and openActionSheet() methods from the component class.
steps.hint: Add two IonButton elements inside the ion-content. Use the (click) event binding to call the component methods.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of adding buttons in Ionic Angular template
<ion-content class="ion-padding">
  <ion-button expand="block" (click)="openModal()">Open Modal</ion-button>
  <ion-button expand="block" (click)="openActionSheet()">Open Action Sheet</ion-button>
</ion-content>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains two buttons that will trigger the modal and action sheet methods when clicked.
successCriteria: The ion-content should contain two IonButton elements with (click) event bindings to openModal() and openActionSheet() methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the buttons that will open the modal and action sheet. The UI now has clear triggers for both features.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some buttons, but make sure you have both buttons with correct (click) event bindings to the component methods.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required buttons with event bindings. Add two IonButton elements inside ion-content with (click)="openModal()" and (click)="openActionSheet()".

steps.title: Add modal button to header
steps.instruction: Inside the ion-toolbar in the template, add an ion-buttons element with slot='end',
steps.hint: Use the ion-buttons component with slot='end' inside ion-toolbar, then add an ion-button with icon='add' and (click)="openModal()".
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Inside an ion-toolbar -->
<ion-buttons slot="end">
  <ion-button (click)="openModal()">
    <ion-icon slot="icon-only" name="add"></ion-icon>
  </ion-button>
</ion-buttons>
steps.expectedOutcome: The header toolbar will have an add button (icon-only) on the right side that triggers the openModal method when clicked.
successCriteria: The template should contain an ion-buttons element with slot='end' inside ion-toolbar, containing an ion-button with (click)="openModal()" and an ion-icon with name='add' and slot='icon-only'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a modal trigger button to the header. The button is positioned at the end of the toolbar and will call the openModal method when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have all required elements: ion-buttons with slot='end', ion-button with (click)="openModal()", and ion-icon with name='add' and slot='icon-only'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button structure is incorrect. Remember to add ion-buttons with slot='end' inside the ion-toolbar, then an ion-button with (click)="openModal()" containing an ion-icon with name='add' and slot='icon-only'.

steps.title: Add action sheet button to content
steps.instruction: Inside the ion-content element, add an ion-button with text 'Open Action Sheet' and an ellipsisHorizontal icon. Wire its (click) event to call the openActionSheet() method.
steps.hint: Add the button inside the ion-content element, using the same pattern as the modal button but with different text and icon.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Inside ion-content -->
<ion-button expand="block" (click)="openActionSheet()">
  <ion-icon slot="start" name="ellipsisHorizontal"></ion-icon>
  Open Action Sheet
</ion-button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The ion-content area now contains a button labeled 'Open Action Sheet' with an ellipsisHorizontal icon that will trigger the action sheet when clicked.
successCriteria: Add an ion-button element inside ion-content with text 'Open Action Sheet', an ellipsisHorizontal icon, and (click)="openActionSheet()" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the action sheet button to the content area. The button is properly wired to call the openActionSheet method when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but it's missing one or more required elements. Make sure it has: 1) text 'Open Action Sheet', 2) an ellipsisHorizontal icon, and 3) (click)="openActionSheet()" event binding.
steps.feedbackWrong: The action sheet button is not correctly implemented. Check that you've added an ion-button inside ion-content with the correct text, icon, and click handler.
